newsitem.title: GERMANY: German insurance body predicts 3 per cent growth.
newsitem.headline: German insurance body predicts 3 per cent growth.

text.p: The German insurance industry is likely to grow by just 3 percent in 1996 to a gross premium income of 232 billion marks, the German insurance federation (GDV) said on Wednesday.
On the eve of its annual meeting on Thursday, the GDV said that this is the lowest growth figure since the second world war. In 1995, insurers had recorded a five percent increase in premium income.

The GDV said that this year's increase is solely due to life and private health insurance, which will go up by 5 percent to 92.8 billion DM (life) and by 7.2 percent to 34.4 billion DM (private health).
Property and casualty lines are likely to see zero growth, remaining static at 96.1 billion DM, the GDV said.
However, the GDV said that this masks different trends. The
motor sector in particular, which is the largest
property/casualty line, is suffering from falling prices and

Insurers expect a drop of 4.5 percent to 42.1 billion marks in the motor sector. Buildings insurance, general liability, household contents insurance and other lines with a focus on private customers are doing better, the GDV said.
German consumers pay an annual 2,130 DM per capita in insurance premiums, a figure which does not include industrial and commercial insurance.

At the same time, contributions to the state social security system amount to 8,250 DM per inhabitant, the GDV said. The trend towards reduced loss frequencies, which started in 1994, is continuing this year, the GDV said. This is true for motor insurance, contents insurance and buildings and plate glass cover.
In the motor insurance sector, the German market was likely to report break-even underwriting figures for 1996. The GDV said that developments in liability were worrying.
Overall, GDV believes that German insurers will achieve
"satisfactory results", due to favourable development of losses and cost savings, and despite falling premium volumes and moderate developments regarding investment income.
